diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: A group of Iranians residing in the UK in Birmingham commemorated the birthday of Empress Farah Pahlavi on Sunday, October 18. A video of the event was sent to Iran International.

The Joint Maritime Information Center announced that a tugboat near Khorfakan was targeted by two unidentified projectiles. Despite damage, the vessel continued on its course. The center also confirmed attacks by the Revolutionary Guard against commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

German police reported a security incident at Leipzig airport, leading to the closure of the northern runway. A vehicle broke through the security fence and entered the airport area on Saturday night. The incident occurred near three Russian Antonov cargo planes that have been grounded since 2022.

The Gulf Cooperation Council condemned the attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia and missile and drone attacks by the Islamic Republic and its proxy forces on member countries and Jordan. The council expressed full solidarity with Saudi Arabia. It also affirmed the right of individual and collective self-defense for its members.

The director general of Kurdistan Environmental Protection announced that 16 alternative prison sentences were issued for environmental offenders during the first six months of this year. These sentences were implemented in Kurdistan province. This information pertains to the current year.

Abbas Kaabi, a member of the Assembly of Experts presidium, stated that revenge against Trump and Netanyahu is certain. He added that legitimate defense and punishing the aggressor are fundamental principles in confronting aggression. He also mentioned that utilizing the country's capacities and people is a way to counter the enemy.
Mohammadmatin Hosseini, a 17-year-old student, was killed on the evening of Friday, January 9, 2026, in Andisheh city, Tehran province. A video of his room was released by his father.

Since the beginning of Mehr 1405, at least 15 women and girls have been killed in various cities in Iran. In many of these murders, relatives of the victims have been identified as perpetrators or suspects. The victims include young girls, mothers, and elderly women.

Hossein Taeb, head of the Basij Organization of the IRGC, stated that one reason the US has not entered a war is the unpredictability of the Islamic Republic's defense methods. He added that the time, place, and means of Iran's response are unknown. US intelligence agencies also consider Iran's response in a potential future war to be unpredictable.

An 800-year-old historic plane tree in the village of Zaglik, Ahar County, was cut down to sell wood and fund the construction of a restroom. The prosecutor of Ahar stated that the tree was cut with coordination from the Fandoglu district office and a legal case is under investigation. The loader used was confiscated and part of the tree trunk was seized.

Sepahan football team drew 0-0 against Shams Azar in the ninth week of the Premier League. Aria Yousefi was sent off in the 32nd minute, and Sepahan played with 10 men for over 60 minutes. With this draw, Sepahan reached 17 points and temporarily moved up to second place in the standings.

Benjamin Netanyahu announced Israel's new national security doctrine emphasizing preemptive strikes and increased weapons production. He stated that the war following the October 7, 2023 attack repelled a nuclear threat against Israel. Netanyahu also highlighted the need to revise security principles and the opportunities for new alliances.

Mokhtar Al-Boshokeh and Hamzeh Savari, two political prisoners, continue their hunger strike and face physical health issues. Al-Boshokeh was transferred from solitary confinement to the general ward in Arak prison. Savari, who is on hunger strike in support of Al-Boshokeh, has experienced low blood pressure.

Prince Reza Pahlavi urged American voters to consider candidates' stance towards the Iranian people and their oppressors in the midterm elections. He called for active participation of Iranians and Americans in the November elections to support Iran's freedom. Pahlavi described the Islamic Republic as the root of the crisis and called for its removal.

Jamshid Barzegar said Donald Trump's support for Benjamin Netanyahu indicates increased coordination between Washington and Tel Aviv to confront the Islamic Republic. He added that the likelihood of new military operations against the Islamic Republic has increased. There is also disagreement in Tehran over negotiation or confrontation with the US.

Workers at Damash mineral water factory reported non-payment of four months of insurance premiums. Despite deductions from their salaries, insurance services have been cut off for about a month. This has caused difficulties for workers and their families in accessing medical treatment.
Thousands of Iranian trucks have stopped at the Pakistan border. This halt has caused problems in traffic and transportation. The reason for the stoppage is not mentioned in the text.

A Malavan fan said the tension at Sirous Ghayeghran Stadium was caused by Shuja Khalilzadeh's controversial gesture during warm-up. Shuja repeated the same gesture he made in Yazd and placed his hand on his groin. This action disrupted the atmosphere in the stadium.

Mehdi Tartaar said that the coaching staff decides on player selection and that Amirhossein Mahmoudi has been training well. He emphasized that the team must make up for lost points in the upcoming match. These remarks were made in a press conference before the game against Mes Shahr-e Babak.

Tariq Metri, Lebanon's Deputy Prime Minister, announced that the country has asked the Islamic Republic to appoint a new ambassador in Beirut. He said they are resolving this diplomatic issue. The ban on Iranian planes landing in Beirut was to prevent an Israeli attack.

Niusha Saremi mentioned Trump's unconditional support for Netanyahu in the audio version of Titrawal. This support coincided with an ultimatum to the Islamic Republic. The topic was released in an audio program.
Egypt and the UAE have entered a regional conflict against Tehran's proxy forces. These developments indicate increased tensions in the region. No further details are provided in the text.

Chris Wright, the US Secretary of Energy, spoke with CNN about the Trump administration's policies towards Iran and the country's security situation. He also announced a decrease in gasoline prices in the US and said he is not satisfied with the current price. Wright explained that the suspension of sanctions related to Lindsey Graham's law does not mean the sanctions are canceled.

Khoddadad Azizi, head of the Tractor team, requested the football federation to take action against Malavan fans after the match was canceled due to their slogans. He stated the match will be held in Tabriz and warned that Tractor fans will act if no action is taken. Azizi is banned from stadiums for four months due to insulting Omid Alishah.

Mehrdad Akhlaghi, the Minister of Defense of the Islamic Republic, stated that the armed forces are ready for war with Israel. He mentioned that future weapons factories will be built in specific locations. These locations must have suitable mountains, secure structures, and appropriate human resources.

Jamshid Barzegar said Donald Trump's support for Benjamin Netanyahu indicates increased coordination between Washington and Tel Aviv against the Islamic Republic. The disputes between Tehran and Washington go beyond the nuclear program, and the likelihood of military operations has increased. The Islamic Republic is trying to prevent a large-scale war by attacking ships and pressuring the energy market.

The Israeli Prime Minister stated that Russia's cooperation with the Islamic Republic is against Israel's interests. He mentioned that Moscow operates networks of anti-Semitic bot accounts and will not leave these actions unanswered. Netanyahu also warned about the danger of a nuclear Iran for Russia.

On October 17 and 18, two workers died in Gorgan and Rasht. Additionally, two workers were injured in Kangan and Tehran. The incidents involved a vehicle collision, falling from a building, a workshop fire, and a hand caught in an industrial meat grinder.

Mehdi Mahdavi-Azad stated in the program "Cheshmandaz" that continuing the Islamic Republic's nuclear policy increases the risk of a third world war. He noted that acquiring nuclear weapons does not necessarily prevent war or the collapse of governments. Mahdavi-Azad described the nuclear program as a tool for maintaining power by part of the regime.

A ceremony for the birthday and flower offering at Farhad Mina's grave was held. This 37-year-old protester was killed on January 9, 2026, in Mashhad. A video of the ceremony was received by Iran International.

At least seven protests were held today, Sunday, 26 Mehr, by Social Security retirees in Kermanshah, Shush, Rasht, Ahvaz, and Tehran, and steel retirees in Isfahan. Yesterday, Lamari car voucher holders also protested due to delays in car delivery. In total, at least seven protests focused on livelihood, healthcare demands, and car delivery follow-ups were reported.

The Israeli Prime Minister thanked Trump for his unconditional support for his re-election and said the cooperation between the two countries to counter the threat of the Islamic Republic continues. He stated that the immediate threat of Tehran obtaining a nuclear bomb has been eliminated, but their joint mission is not yet complete. Netanyahu emphasized that this cooperation is vital for Israel's survival and linked it to the election outcome.
At 00:29, two explosion sounds were reported in Konarak. Multiple messages confirm this incident. The source of this news is Vahid Online.

Hamzeh Darvish, a Sunni prisoner, is being held in Suite 35 of Qezelhesar Prison in Karaj after his transfer. After 23 days without phone contact, he made a brief call to his family but remains deprived of regular visits and calls. Hamzeh ended his hunger strike after one week.

Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, stated that Benjamin Netanyahu is dragging the US into another war without considering the consequences. He warned the US that Iran is stronger than before and ready to respond. These remarks were made in reaction to Donald Trump's threats.

Videos published on social media show the destruction of cafes on the coastal boulevard of Khorramshahr along the Karun River. Corniche Cafe, Livan Cafe, and Strawberry Cafe are among the destroyed places.

The match between Malavan and Tractor in the ninth week of the Iranian Premier League was canceled due to fans' chants. Accounts of the reasons and the final decision are contradictory. Mazdak Mirzaei interviewed Mohammad Taghavi on the Hat-trick program.
Tractor football players left the field after fans' chants and pre-match tensions. The match at Sirous Ghaeqran Stadium in Anzali was not held. This incident led to the cancellation of the game.

Real Madrid defeated Sevilla 4-1 in the ninth week of La Liga with a double from Kylian Mbappe and goals from Arda Guler and Yan Diumande. This victory brought Mourinho's team to 21 points, keeping them in third place in the standings. The absence of Vinicius was not felt in this home win for Real Madrid.

Morad Vaisi stated that Netanyahu announced a new Israeli security doctrine. He said Netanyahu has instructed security agencies to overthrow the Islamic Republic. This is the most significant confrontation in 48 years.

Donald Trump stated that Russia provides very little help to the Islamic Republic of Iran compared to its capabilities, and he wants to maintain this situation. He also said he does not intend to harm the peace negotiations for Ukraine by actions that would push Moscow away from the negotiation table. Trump added that significant progress has been made in negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine war.

US President Donald Trump, nine days before Israel's election, declared full support for Benjamin Netanyahu and warned that if Tehran does not change its behavior, the US will 'finish the job'. Netanyahu welcomed the support and stressed the continuation of the joint mission against the Islamic Republic. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi responded that Tehran has 'unfinished business' with the US.

Reza Pahlavi urged Iranians living in the US to participate in the November elections and consider Iran's freedom in their decision-making. He emphasized that a free Iran can contribute to US security, economy, and global stability. Political analyst Navid Mohibi said Pahlavi is trying to highlight the importance of the Strait of Hormuz's security and the energy market to US politicians.
Murad Vaisi stated in the audio version of the policy that Trump gave the green light to Israel for a joint attack.

Tensions continued in Paris one day after nationwide protests against rising living costs, with police clashing with protesters. Nearly 2,400 people were arrested and about a thousand police and gendarmerie officers were injured during Saturday's unrest. Emmanuel Macron condemned the uncontrolled violence and promised increased security measures.

Ali Abdollahi, Chief of Staff of Iran's Armed Forces, warned that any renewed attack on Iran will be met with a stronger response. He stated that any miscalculation by the US and Israel will face a severe reaction. These remarks come amid ongoing verbal tensions between Iran, the US, and Israel.

The foreign ministers of the Gulf Cooperation Council member states called for a return to dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the crisis with the Islamic Republic. They emphasized that any agreement should include Tehran's nuclear, missile, and drone programs as well as support for proxy forces. They also condemned missile and drone attacks by the Islamic Republic and its proxy forces.

The virtual US embassy in Iran warned that the Islamic Republic and its supporting groups may target American interests and centers. It urged American citizens to leave Iran and prepare for flight cancellations and travel disruptions. It also advised avoiding large gatherings.

Gulf countries have continued investing in the natural gas sector despite increased defense and reconstruction costs. Since early 2026, projects worth about 50 billion dollars have been approved. Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and the UAE are among the leading investors.

Mohammad Reza Naqdi stated that the country's missile centers were unharmed during recent bombings and strategic reserves remain intact. He said the US Fifth Fleet has withdrawn from its bases in Bahrain. Naqdi also claimed that over 240 enemy aircraft have been destroyed in this war.

Mohammad Rashidi, a member of the parliament's board, said that the main goal of US pressures is to create a negative outlook on Iran's economic future. He added that the Americans aimed to quickly see the effects of the pressures through repeated claims and deadlines. Additionally, the US tries to create worry and anxiety in society by exaggerating the pressures.

Abbas Araghchi reacted to Macron's remarks about the impact of fuel prices caused by the Iran war on protests in France, accusing Macron of creating the conditions for this situation. He said Macron assured the US president of support for crimes against Iranians. Araghchi added that the French people demand fundamental changes, including guarantees for freedom of assembly.

The president of the University of Tehran announced the formation of a working group to address student dress code issues. This group invites students confidentially and tries to resolve matters without referring them to the disciplinary council. The university also strictly deals with tobacco use on campus.

The Israeli army announced that in attacks in the Gaza Strip, a Hamas cell commander and two members of its military wing were killed. These individuals were involved in planning attacks against Israel and rebuilding Hamas's military capabilities. The airstrikes took place in the Al-Daraj, Al-Tuffah, and Jabalia areas.

The Israeli Prime Minister described Iran's nuclear program as the greatest threat to Israel. He warned that a single nuclear bomb could kill hundreds of thousands in Israel. This issue is cited as one of the reasons for a military attack on Iran.

The director of the Kerman Standards Office announced criminal charges against 23 unsafe elevators. These elevators did not comply with safety requirements or failed to address reported defects. Municipalities are not allowed to issue completion certificates for elevators without standard approval.

Sadegh Beigdeli referred to recent threats by Iranian officials against Israel. He said that while public positions are harsh, different messages are sent in behind-the-scenes negotiations. Beigdeli believes Iran's efforts to maintain appearances in negotiations seem to be failing.

Iranians living in Calgary, Canada, held a protest against executions by the Islamic Republic. The gathering took place in front of the city hall. They demanded to raise the voice of the Iranian people to the international community.

People report issues such as drug shortages, unpaid wages and benefits, and rising living and rent costs. Some oil workers and retired telecommunications employees complain about not receiving their dues. Daily expenses like meat, travel, and even fruit have significantly decreased.

Citizens have received text messages threatening legal action and monitoring their activities on social media. The sender cited the Islamic Penal Code, stating that the citizen's actions in approving and spreading criminal content are under investigation. These messages were sent from the number of the Intelligence Organization of FARAJA.

Asia Times wrote that the war between the US and the Islamic Republic and the Middle East oil crisis have entered a new phase of competition between Washington and Beijing. This situation may weaken Trump's position ahead of the midterm elections. Additionally, increasing instability in the region could threaten China's interests and Xi Jinping's plans.

Seven defendants, including two women, in Mashhad were sentenced to death, imprisonment, and 74 lashes for charges including murder, theft, and kidnapping. These sentences were issued by the Fifth Branch of the Criminal Court One of Khorasan Razavi Province.

Parviz Sarvari, deputy chairman of Tehran City Council, stated that the Islamic Republic can target Europe and the USA, and missile range is no longer limited. He warned that if Europe follows US policies against Iran, it will have to pay the price. Sarvari also mentioned the possibility of moving towards a regional war.

Rouhollah Rahimpour mentioned Trump's support for Netanyahu and said that if Netanyahu wins, the likelihood of a joint military action by the US and Israel against the Islamic Republic will increase. He added that military confrontation with Tehran may become Netanyahu's main foreign policy agenda.

Mohammad Mokhber said Mojtaba Khamenei has mastery over governance and military issues. He added that Mojtaba Khamenei's succession has brought peace back to the country. Mokhber described the country's future as bright.
Amin Ghodousian, a citizen of Rask county, has been detained by intelligence officers in Chabahar for six days. His place of detention is still unknown.

A citizen reported that the door of Dabiri School in Chaldoran, West Azerbaijan province, has been closed. The head of education stated that the school door will not be opened for preschoolers because no contract has been signed.

An Austrian passenger plane en route from Tel Aviv to Vienna made an emergency landing at Sofia airport due to a bomb threat. All 57 passengers were safely evacuated. Security investigations into the source of the threat are ongoing.

Mostafa Khoshcheshm, a political analyst from IRIB, stated that Europe could be targeted by missile attacks if necessary. He also mentioned that the Islamic Republic might have more bombs. These remarks were published by Iran International.

Benjamin Netanyahu expressed gratitude for Donald Trump's support. He said Israel has never had a greater friend than Trump in the White House. Netanyahu added that Trump is bravely working to eliminate the nuclear threat from the Islamic Republic against the US and Israel.

Hadi Khanari-Nejad was elected as the president of the Gymnastics Federation with 35 out of 38 votes. Initially, five candidates were qualified, but three withdrew. Habib Nozohouri also withdrew before presenting his program, and the election continued with a single candidate.

Marco Rubio called the Islamic Republic the main cause of instability in the Middle East. He said Donald Trump destroyed much of Iran's military capability. He also stated that US sanctions reduce the Islamic Republic's financial resources.

A group of Iranians gathered on Sunday, 26 Mehr, in front of the UK Prime Minister's office in London. They protested against executions by the Islamic Republic and showed support for Prince Reza Pahlavi. The video was released by Iran International.

Marco Rubio, the US Secretary of State, said in an interview that Hezbollah is 100% backed by Iran and Shiite militias in Iraq are supported by the Islamic Republic. He added that Iran has directly attacked several regional countries and is the main supporter of the Houthis. Rubio emphasized that to resolve instability in the Middle East, the root cause must be identified and confronted.

A group of retired telecommunications workers in Kurdistan province held a protest today. They protested against the insurance situation and the performance of the Executive Headquarters of Imam's Directive and the Cooperative Foundation of the IRGC in the telecommunications company. The protest was held in response to the current conditions.
Amin Dehestani, a blogger residing in Khorramabad, was arrested and transferred to prison to serve a two-year sentence. This occurred on Sunday, 26 Mehr 1405. Harana News Agency reported this news.

The German Foreign Ministry summoned the Iranian ambassador due to an attempt to attack two leaders of the Jewish community in Germany. This action followed a Hamburg High Court ruling regarding the Quds Force's attempt to spy and plan terrorist operations. Germany stated that it will not tolerate attacks on Jews.

Ashkan Pourrashid, owner of Malavan club, called for an impartial investigation into the cancellation of the match against Tractor. He warned that if unlawful pressures influence the match result, he will withdraw from football. Pourrashid also denied allegations of racist chants in Anzali stadium and requested evidence.

The head of traffic engineering at Tehran's traffic police announced that out of 349 accident-prone points in the capital, 175 remain unsecured. Some of these points have not been addressed for years. Accident-prone points on highways require urgent attention due to traffic conditions.

Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's foreign minister, responded to Abbas Araghchi's remarks about the protests in France, saying the Iranian foreign minister is happy about the unrest in France. He also referred to Iran's internal repression and executions. Araghchi had earlier called for guarantees of freedom of assembly in France.

A video shows the first presence of the missing family of Alireza Raeisi at his grave in the deserts of Anarak, Isfahan province. Alireza Raeisi, cousin of Ramin Raeisi, was one of the killed protesters in December protests in Isfahan. He was executed on October 5, 2026, along with Alireza Sepahi.

During the protests on October 17 in Grenoble, France, a group of protesters hijacked a small tourist train and moved it through the city center streets. The protesters then abandoned the train towards the police forces. This incident was reported during the protests.

Tractor club issued a statement claiming that its players and fans were targeted by ethnic and racist slogans and demanded decisive action from the football federation. The club's owner decided not to have the team appear on the field based on football federation regulations regarding racist slogans. The club emphasized that the time for repeated condemnations and empty promises is over.
Mohsen Moloudpour, a citizen from Oshnavieh, was arrested by security forces on Saturday, October 17. His detention location is unknown. This news was reported by Harana News Agency.

Reports have emerged about bribery among judges in Kermanshah and rising prices of motor oil. There are also issues with salary payments at the Khuzestan oil company and dissatisfaction with the ration card system in Tehran. People complain about inflation, poor internet quality, and healthcare difficulties.
A citizen in Rudsar was arrested for writing posts on social media, which the police described as insulting martyrs and disturbing public opinion.

Ali Abbasi, the police commander of Masjed Soleyman, announced the arrest of a person who injured a doctor with a cold weapon. The incident occurred last night in a medical clinic. The motive of the accused was stated to be previous disputes.

A group of victims of the Pishgaman cooperative company in Yazd gathered in front of the company's office on Monday, October 19. They protested due to months of uncertainty and unclear profits and capital. The gathering was held to express dissatisfaction with the company's situation.

The German Foreign Ministry summoned the Iranian ambassador following a Hamburg court ruling against two suspects accused of spying for the Islamic Republic. The two were convicted of planning attacks on two prominent Jewish and pro-Israel figures and sentenced to a total of 13 years in prison. More details are available in an interview with an Iran International reporter.

Amnesty International has examined the repression network and command structure of the Islamic Republic during the "Woman, Life, Freedom" uprising in a detailed report. Morteza Kazemian explains the pillars of repression and the consequences of the deaths of dozens of security and military officials. The report investigates crimes against humanity.

Shervin Asbaghian, the Deputy of Sports at the Ministry of Sports and Youth, commented on the controversy surrounding the Malavan and Tractor match, stating these teams are valuable assets of the country's football. He added that global arrogance does not want peace in the country. Managers and fans of these teams are aware and will not allow the country's peace to be disturbed.
Emmanuel Macron, President of France, and Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah, Emir of Kuwait, signed agreements at Bayan Palace in Kuwait.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh said Donald Trump's support for Benjamin Netanyahu indicates the future path of the US government. He added that the joint US-Israel project can only be military. Also, Washington excludes Israel from negotiations if it chooses the negotiation path.

Female workers in home cleaning services face issues such as lack of insurance, job insecurity, and unpaid wages. The use of chemical detergents and harsh working conditions have caused physical injuries. Some of these women have had to quit their jobs due to physical and social problems.

The director of forensic medicine in West Azerbaijan announced that 656 workers were injured due to work-related accidents in the first six months of this year. Among them, 636 were men and 20 were women.

The 70th London International Film Festival was held from October 7 to 18. In this edition, 251 works from 88 countries were screened. Six Iranian films addressing themes such as protest, censorship, and migration participated in the festival.

A missile attack by the Houthis on a military training camp in Shabwah province killed at least 18 people. A projectile hit a residential area in Najran, Saudi Arabia, injuring six. Houthi media reported 9 deaths in a Saudi airstrike on Saada.

Reza Akbari Adel and Mohammad Esmaeili Alafi, two lawyers from the East Azerbaijan Bar Association, were arrested after being summoned to the Tabriz Prosecutor's Office. They have been transferred to an unknown location, and authorities have not provided information about the reasons for their arrest. This arrest occurred on October 18.

The Iranian national freestyle wrestling team under 23 years old won the world championship in Las Vegas with four gold, one silver, and four bronze medals. The team scored 180 points, ranking above Russia and the USA. This report was provided by Mehdi Rostampour.

Protesters threw incendiary materials on the sixth day of protests in Tirana. These protests are against government corruption, unemployment, and weaknesses in the education system. Police reported that 388 people have been prosecuted and dozens have been injured.

Amir Mohammad Hatami, an 18-year-old from Shahin Shahr, Isfahan, was killed by a fatal gunshot after being wounded and arrested on the night of January 9. His family identified his tortured body after 20 days of searching. Amir Mohammad worked as a mechanic and was known as a kind and responsible young man.
Sergey Lavrov, the Russian Foreign Minister, traveled to Tehran on Monday, 27 Mehr. During this trip, he met with Abbas Araghchi, the Iranian Foreign Minister. The meeting took place in Tehran.

Samad Hassanzadeh, head of the Chamber of Commerce, warned about the social and economic consequences of stagflation. Arash Azarmi from Iran International said the country is experiencing the worst stagflation in 80 years. Economic activists have warned of widespread economic crises.

With the start of the fifth week of protests in France, clashes continue in various cities. Iranian photojournalist Alfred Yaghoubzadeh was injured while covering the protests in Paris. This incident occurred on October 17.

Fatemeh Ayni, a female prisoner sentenced to death for drug-related crimes, was transferred to solitary confinement in Lakan Prison in Rasht. She is 31 years old and resides in Karaj. Her transfer was for the execution of the death sentence.

Rashad Muhammad Al-Alimi, head of Yemen's leadership council, asked Antonio Guterres to support an international action to list the Houthis as a terrorist organization. He also called for a ban on arms shipments and cutting financial resources to the Houthis. Guterres condemned the Houthi attacks and emphasized support for the Yemeni government.

Some citizens have reported the cutoff of subsidies and ration cards and being deprived of increased livelihood assistance. Groups such as the disabled, retirees, unemployed, and female heads of households have been excluded from receiving government support. This issue was discussed in an interview with Seba Heydarkhani.

A couple was sitting on a cafe terrace near the Arc de Triomphe in Paris amid ongoing unrest. The unrest followed the joining of students, labor unions, and Yellow Vest movement members in protests against price increases. Flames from a burning trash can were visible in the background.

France is once again experiencing street unrest, which reminds Iranians of the 1979 revolution. These developments refer to the coalition of leftists and Islamists and its consequences for Iran. Adaleh Borang has commented on social media users' reactions to this issue.

Amirhossein Sheikhmohammadi, a veterinary student at Azad University of Karaj, has been detained since May 17, 2026, and needs medical treatment but is denied access to healthcare services. His trial has not yet been held and the date is unknown. He is also deprived of access to a lawyer and medical leave.

The Iranian sports team won 8 medals, including 3 gold, 3 silver, and 2 bronze, on the first day of the 2026 Nagoya Para Asian Games. Ailar Jami, Elham Salehi, and Sina Zighaminejad won gold medals for Iran. Iran ranked seventh in the overall competition table.

Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei, head of the judiciary, called Donald Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu "heartless and foolish." He said these individuals resorted to threatening the Iranian people out of desperation. He also emphasized that the Iranian nation is not afraid of terror or war and will not retreat.

Seven detainees from the December 2025 protests were sentenced by Tehran Revolutionary Court to a total of 60 years and six months in prison. The individuals include Amir Sabaghi, Abedin Golshani, Samira Mohibi, and others. Samira Mohibi is held in Qarchak Varamin prison, while the others are in Greater Tehran prison.

A blind citizen reported that after transferring his case, his pension and livelihood assistance have been cut off for seven months. He currently receives only 400,000 tomans in subsidies and one million tomans in commodity basket credit. Additionally, the registration system for increasing commodity basket credit lacks an option for incomes below 20 million tomans.

Abbas Araghchi stated that cooperation between Iran and Russia will play an important role in regional stability. Diplomatic consultations between Tehran and Moscow continue at the highest level. Lavrov explained Moscow's plan for a collective security system in the Persian Gulf.

Persepolis football team defeated Mes Shahr-e Babak 3-0 in the ninth week of the Iranian Premier League. The goals were scored by Tiwi Bifouma, Majid Eidi, and Mohammad Hossein Sadeghi. With this win, Persepolis reached 20 points and topped the league table.

The Islamic Republic announced that over 31 million people have registered in the "Jan Fada" campaign. The commanders of the IRGC and Basij have reported the start of training volunteers and forming new battalions. The purpose of organizing these forces is still unclear.
Milan city center witnessed violence for the second consecutive day. Groups of young people attacked stores and damaged public and private property. Clashes with police forces also occurred.

Homayoun Shabankareh, a 22-year-old prisoner in Karaj, was sentenced to death on charges of waging war and espionage. The sentence was issued by the second branch of the Revolutionary Court of Karaj. The death sentence was communicated to him on Saturday, October 17.

Seven detainees from the Iranian National Revolution in December 1404 were sentenced to prison terms ranging from one to 21 years. Charges include operational actions against national security and propaganda against the regime. They are held in different prisons, and their case is linked to Borzou Rezaei, who was sentenced to death.

Telecommunications retirees in Hamadan, Rasht, and Bijar held protests alongside retirees in several cities. They protested against the performance of the Executive Headquarters of Imam's Order and the Cooperative Foundation of the IRGC. Retirees in Bijar demanded salary adjustments and the implementation of the Supreme Administrative Court's unified ruling 9235.

A cafe and two women's hair salons in Jiroft were closed due to non-compliance with Islamic codes of conduct. This action was taken for specific reasons. More details are available in the Harana news agency.

The tariff war between the US and Canada has strained trade relations. The issue of Alberta's separation from Canada has become a significant political topic. On October 19, a vote will be held to start the legal process for a binding referendum on separation.

Mehrdad Akhlaghi, Iran's defense minister, stated at his introduction ceremony that current conditions require addressing the needs of the armed forces. He emphasized that defense ministry activities must continue without interruption and that a meeting was held with the IRGC Aerospace Force commander. He also highlighted improving the living conditions of armed forces personnel and their families as a key management priority.
A video shows a group of students in an Iranian school tearing and trampling images of Ruhollah Khomeini from textbooks. This video was received by Iran International.

Vahid Vidafer, a resident of Tabriz, remains detained in Tabriz prison without a clear status after 75 days. He was arrested on August 5. The reason for his arrest was liking a post on Benjamin Netanyahu's page.

Sheikh Saud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani announced that Qatar will soon establish a defense equipment production center domestically. Qatar is cooperating with regional partners and the US, UK, and France to develop its domestic defense capabilities. The country will also invest in companies active in the defense sector.

Amirhossein Sheikhmohammadi, a student at Azad University of Karaj, has been detained for five months in Choubinder Prison in Qazvin. He has been deprived of specialized medical care and phone contact with his family. His case remains unresolved and no court session has been held yet.
